title: USMCA/CUSMA annual joint review — the first of the yearly cycle the US triggered by declining to extend
source: EST: derived from the anniversary rule, not read off a published schedule. USMCA art. 34.7 fixes the first joint review on the sixth anniversary of entry into force (2020-07-01 -> 2026-07-01); the US did not confirm it wished to extend at that meeting (USTR press statement of 2026-07, Ambassador Greer; White & Case alert 'USMCA 2026 Joint Review: United States declines to extend Agreement, triggering annual reviews', natlawreview carry fetched 2026-09-09), which activates art. 34.7.4 — a joint review EVERY YEAR until the parties agree to extend or the Agreement reaches its 16-year term on 2036-07-01. Canada's own international.gc.ca joint-review page (fetched direct 2026-09-09) confirms the 2020-07-01 entry into force, the 2026-07-01 first review and the 2036 term. The IMPLEMENTING STATUTE is primary and was read: 19 U.S.C. 4611 speaks of 'any subsequent annual joint review meeting conducted as required under article 34.7 of the USMCA' and hangs a 70-day-prior US consultation obligation off it (uscode.house.gov, fetched direct 2026-09-09)
notes: PROPOSED AS AN ESTIMATE WITH A KNOWN SOFT SPOT IN THE DATE, STATED UP FRONT: no source fetched this session names 2027-07-01 explicitly. Art. 34.7.4 says the reviews are annual; every secondary read (White & Case, natlawreview, joffroy, ICPA) says 'annually' and anchors the cycle to the July 1 anniversary; 19 U.S.C. 4611 calls it a 'meeting' with a 70-day-prior US consultation step, i.e. a convened event whose day the Free Trade Commission sets. So the YEAR is solid, the MONTH is well supported by the anniversary rule, and the DAY is derived. Treat as estimate in the strong sense — it widens caution, it does not license date-keyed action, and a session that finds a published 2027 review date or a Federal Register consultation notice (the derived ~2027-04-22 lead date from the 70-day rule is NOT proposed, since it depends on a meeting date that is itself derived) should amend it. WHY THE CANADA COUNTER-TARIFF LANE FILED IT: closing out canada-counter-tariffs-effective-2026-09-08 established that the 2026 US-Canada tariff exchange has NO dated forward hook of its own — neither instrument carries a review, sunset or scheduled negotiation, and Carney's 2026-09-03 'we're ready to sit down... when the Americans are ready' is undated. The annual joint review is therefore the only scheduled venue at which the tariff wall between the two largest USMCA parties is institutionally on the table, and it is the natural place for either a settlement or a further escalation to surface. It is also the single largest untracked trade-policy date on this calendar's horizon: preferential tariffs, rules of origin, investment protections and dispute settlement for ~US$1.8T of annual North American trade all sit inside the agreement being reviewed. Filed medium, not high: the review is a scheduled check-in that changes no obligation by itself (Canada's own page: 'not an expiry date, but rather a scheduled check-in'), all USMCA rights remain fully operative through it, and the 2026 edition passed with no measurable market reaction. Discovered during the canada-counter-tariffs-effective-2026-09-08 close-out (2026-09-09).
